canonical_policy_sections.heading: EXECUTION CONTRACT
canonical_policy_sections.text:
## EXECUTION CONTRACT
Accept one original RCT PDF. Read entire Methods, Results, tables, captions, figures, supplementary text, and footnotes. Extract into the companion JSON data contract, validate structure and scientific semantics, and export a single .xlsx. The first worksheet must be **Master Excel Sheet**, followed by **Studies, Arms, Eligibility, Baseline, Outcomes, Sources, Validation Log, QA Inventory**. The first worksheet may show *read-only views* of source records but must not create additional analytical observations. Preserve machine-readable IDs and avoid merged cells in tables. Store absent JSON quantities as null and write genuine empty Excel cells. A missing value is not zero and must not appear as NA, NR, N/A, dash, or fabricated overall values.

canonical_policy_sections.heading: ORIGINAL RULES
canonical_policy_sections.text:
## ORIGINAL RULES 

**Rule 01 — No duplicates.** IF the same outcome appears in abstract, text, table and figure, THEN store a single unique observation linked to every source; DO NOT duplicate efficacy or adverse-event data. Preserve different arm, dose, comparison, population, assessment stage, endpoint definition, observation period, or estimate type as separate genuine observations.

**Rule 02 — Atomic cells.** IF a source reports 65 years, THEN store numeric 65 and unit years in separate cells. Multiword clinical categories (e.g. type 2 diabetes) remain intact as one categorical field. Do not split them letter by letter or word by word.

**Rule 03 — Separate comparison operators.** IF a criterion says age ≥ 18 years, THEN store `lower_operator_1='>'`, `lower_operator_2='='`, `lower_value=18`, and `unit='years'` in distinct cells. Distinguish >, ≥, <, ≤ and =. Do not silently change direction.

**Rule 04 — Split ranges.** IF lower/upper thresholds exist, THEN store lower/upper numbers, both operator components, and unit separately. Record inclusion or exclusion of each endpoint; do not silently treat exclusive bounds as inclusive.

**Rule 05 — Missing data.** IF not explicitly supported by source THEN JSON null / truly blank Excel value; do not substitute 0, NA, em dash or invented data. Record unverifiable extraction as a validation issue.

**Rule 06 — Full PDF coverage.** Search Abstract, Methods, Results, all tables, figures, footnotes and supplements. Cross-check overlapping reports. Preserve conflicts as unresolved flags, not silently resolved guesses.

**Rule 07 — First worksheet and sections.** Name first worksheet exactly `Master Excel Sheet`; organize Study & Arms, Eligibility, Baseline, Efficacy, Safety in that order. Additional normalized sheets hold the authoritative unique records.

**Rule 08 — Study metadata.** Capture title, authors, journal, year, DOI, registration, location, design, randomization, blinding, centers, sample sizes, duration, trial phase ONLY IF stated, objectives, endpoints and funding. Never infer phase from dose or sample size.

**Rule 09 — All arms.** Capture every randomized arm (including placebo), separate distinct doses, units, route, frequency, duration, allocated N, analyzed N. IF dose/frequency is absent THEN leave blank, including for placebo; do not write arbitrary 0 mg.

**Rule 10 — Eligibility from Methods.** Locate participant selection and inclusion/exclusion from methods, screening, washout, run-in and supplement; abstract alone is insufficient.

**Rule 11 — Inclusion and exclusion separated.** Every criterion must explicitly be `INCLUSION` or `EXCLUSION` with separate records and distinct section headers in the Master Excel Sheet. Preserve original wording and its structured interpretation.

**Rule 12 — Drug restrictions specific.** IF publication names drug classes, named medications, exclusions or exceptions THEN preserve exact examples; never generalize to 'all diabetes medications'.

**Rule 13 — Duration and medication context.** Preserve stability, use, discontinuation, washout intervals, thresholds and units with separate operator/value/unit columns.

**Rule 14 — Eligibility subgroups and stage.** IF thresholds differ by drug-naive/prior-treatment subgroup or screening/run-in THEN represent separately with population_subgroup and assessment_stage. Never merge HbA1c cutoffs across stages.

**Rule 15 — Complete baseline.** Review baseline tables and footnotes; include all actually reported demographic, disease, laboratory, medication and comorbidity characteristics.

**Rule 16 — Population scope.** IF a categorical property explicitly applies to every participant (e.g. Japanese study population), it may be repeated as a shared context on each arm, WITH overall provenance. IF an age mean, race proportion or count is only reported overall, keep it overall, not falsely arm-specific.

**Rule 17 — Blank cells not 'same as above'.** Fill genuinely applicable arm-context fields explicitly; only leave data blank if source is silent. Never use merged data cells.

**Rule 18 — Preserve summary statistics.** Mean and SD are separate numeric cells; median, quartiles, range, count, and percentage remain separate fields. Do not transform median to mean or CI to SD without justified, separately logged methods.

**Rule 19 — All endpoints.** Extract primary/secondary efficacy and harms, retaining any other author-defined outcome domain.

**Rule 20 — Exhaustive tables.** For every relevant table entry check endpoint, arm, comparator, denominator, units, estimate type, timepoint and statistical annotations.

**Rule 21 — Figure extraction.** Read figure title, axis names/units, scale, panel, legend, caption and annotations BEFORE mapping values. Printed labels may be exact. Graphically estimated unprinted values must be marked approximate and flagged unless source confirms them.

**Rule 22 — No endpoint reassignment.** FPG, PPG AUC, 24h CGM glucose, MAGE and HbA1c are distinct constructs. Reject any value mapped to the wrong endpoint, arm or dose.

**Rule 23 — Estimate semantics.** Distinguish RAW_MEAN, MEAN_CHANGE, ADJUSTED_MEAN_CHANGE, ADJUSTED_MEAN_DIFFERENCE, RAW_MEAN_DIFFERENCE and relative effects. Do not store adjusted changes as `mean_sd` absent an actual SD. Identify effect direction, arm and comparator.

**Rule 24 — Confidence intervals.** Record point estimate, CI lower, CI upper, level, units and P-value/operator as separate atomic fields, without losing negative signs or decimal precision.

**Rule 25 — Timepoint semantics.** Preserve original label and numeric day/period if unambiguous. Day 1, Day 2, Day 28 and Day 29 cannot be substituted. Safety observation periods are not point measurements; distinguish treatment day and assessment day.

**Rule 26 — Safety extraction.** Preserve event label, arm, N participants with event, denominator, %, seriousness, grade, relation and observation period. Events are not participants; 'any AE' is not the sum of named events unless source establishes nonoverlap.

**Rule 27 — Independent second pass.** Revisit original PDF for every record; verify exact value, sign, dose, arm, endpoint, effect type, comparator, CI, unit, timepoint and provenance, plus every duplicated-looking record.

**Rule 28 — PDF is primary reference.** When extracted workbook conflicts with original paper, do not prefer system-generated QA scores or previous workbook values; correct from PDF and log change.

**Rule 29 — Field-level provenance.** Provide source IDs with page, section/table/figure/panel, snippet and extraction method. Every verified observation must point to readable source evidence.

**Rule 30 — Validation log.** For every error store rule ID, record ID, original interpretation, proposed correction, source, severity and resolution status. Unresolved material issues must prevent PASS.

**Rule 31 — PICO.** Capture Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcome; document actual comparisons instead of generating every possible arm-vs-arm contrast.

**Rule 32 — PRISMA alignment.** Preserve study selection/effect-result descriptors useful later, but PRISMA is a systematic-review reporting framework, not a validator of an individual RCT.

**Rule 33 — CONSORT alignment.** Extract reported participant flow, sequence generation, concealment, blinding, attrition, harms and N analyzed; do not infer unreported methodological compliance.

**Rule 34 — Quality gate.** Verify all arms/eligibility/baseline/outcomes/safety, unique identities, no unsupported or swapped assignments, schema format, missingness and provenance. Flag any source uncertainty.

**Rule 35 — Deliverable.** Export exactly one machine-readable workbook with first sheet Master Excel Sheet plus normalized source data and validation log. Export structured JSON conforming to `MANDOROS_Phase1_Strict_Schema.json` as a companion intermediate dataset.

canonical_policy_sections.text:
## STRICT SEMANTIC VALIDATION — MACHINE CHECKS + PDF REVIEW

V01: Validate JSON against Draft 2020-12 schema; reject unknown fields, missing required keys, bad enumerations, numeric strings in numeric fields, and extra undeclared properties.
V02: Primary keys unique within each table; every arm_id and source_id reference exists. For single RCT, one study object only.
V03: A study contains all and only source-confirmed randomized arms. If 3 arms reported, 3 arms present with correct N. Group randomized counts must sum to total randomized N when all are reported for the same flow stage; missing values are not failures of arithmetic.
V04: Study arms cannot imply placebo has numeric 0 mg unless paper reports such a numeric dose; treatment frequency 'daily' belongs in period unit while frequency number is numeric.
V05: All published inclusion/exclusion thresholds and stage-specific criteria preserved; preserve named medication exceptions and minimum/maximum operators.
V06: Baseline scope check: overall data never copied into arm-level numerical estimates; categorical shared context may be repeated only with explicit whole-cohort source statement.
V07: Unique outcome key = study, endpoint precise definition, domain, arm, comparator, analysis population, timepoint or observation period, estimate_type, subgroup and safety severity where applicable. A citation source does NOT make an outcome unique.

**Rule 05 — Missing data.** IF not explicitly supported by source THEN JSON null / truly blank Excel value; do not substitute 0, NA, em dash or invented data. Record unverifiable extraction as a validation issue.

additional_system_implementation_rules.title: Preserve prior rules and architecture
additional_system_implementation_rules.then: Apply every relevant embedded Phase 1 extraction, schema and validation rule before additional synthesis steps; preserve existing features and worksheets; never silently alter them.

additional_system_implementation_rules.title: One RCT or multiple reports is not meta-analysis
additional_system_implementation_rules.if: Less than two independent studies contribute to a proposed pooled estimate
additional_system_implementation_rules.then: Show one-study estimates and confidence intervals when valid; do not create pooled multi-study effects, Cochran Q, I2, tau2, pooled weight, publication-bias estimates or prediction intervals.

additional_system_implementation_rules.title: Study-vs-report deduplication
additional_system_implementation_rules.if: Two PDFs share registry, participant population or trial identity
additional_system_implementation_rules.then: Link reports to one study_id; extract complementary data without double counting study participants.

additional_system_implementation_rules.title: Source-level semantic provenance
additional_system_implementation_rules.if: Any value is considered for pooling
additional_system_implementation_rules.then: Verify exact PDF page, table/figure, arm, comparator, population, outcome definition, timepoint, estimate type, numerical value, scale and CI before approving.

additional_system_implementation_rules.title: Statistical computation
additional_system_implementation_rules.if: A study effect or pooled estimate must be calculated
additional_system_implementation_rules.then: Run reproducible audited statistical code with recorded package/version/method/assumptions; do not use a language model as the numerical calculation engine.

additional_system_implementation_rules.title: Preserve missingness
additional_system_implementation_rules.if: No valid SD, SE, CI or independent group variance information exists
additional_system_implementation_rules.then: Leave missing values null, record verification status, refrain from inventing numbers; do not pool unless justified derivation or compatible data are available.

additional_system_implementation_rules.title: Prevent analytical contamination
additional_system_implementation_rules.if: Records are projections, simulations, virtual cohorts or AI predictions
additional_system_implementation_rules.then: Isolate them with explicit origin labels and exclude from systematic-review pooling unless separately authorized in a simulation workflow.

additional_system_implementation_rules.title: Eligibility and subgroup meanings
additional_system_implementation_rules.if: Eligibility differs by screening/run-in or prior treatment history
additional_system_implementation_rules.then: Retain subgroup, time stage and threshold operators; do not homogenize distinct HbA1c conditions.

additional_system_implementation_rules.title: False assurance prevention
additional_system_implementation_rules.if: Any source mapping error, wrong dose/time, duplicated participants or irreproducible effect remains
additional_system_implementation_rules.then: Set final acceptance REJECTED or MANUAL_REVIEW regardless of self-reported score; 100/100 only means all predefined applicable tests passed.
